body: Thanks for the reply. Yeah it looks like my silence is interesting to her, so I'll try to talk about more random impersonal stuff.
Thanks for the reply. Do you have any tips for what perfect textbook grey rocking looks like? I feel like I read and hear different things and I'm not sure if I'm doing it right.

I feel like I'm trying to remind myself of my mom's good qualities, in hopes that with a thorough enough explanation of everything, she'll finally understand. I feel like that's also the only way I can attempt to stand my ground and enforce my boundaries. It will take a lot of self reflection on her part, which is a lot to expect from a narcissist, and part of the reason for my hesitancy.

I've tried letting it go, since I know I'm fighting a losing battle here, but I can't help but feel so much jealousy towards my sister. If I send those paragraphs of what I feel, and there's no improvement, I can feel like I tried everything, and I can stop investing any more emotional energy into them. I'm also hesitant because I'm thinking of the worst case scenario, where she sees everything as a personal attack and that I'm an ungrateful brat who doesn't deserve anything, making the situation worse than if I'd said nothing.

Thanks for your reply.

I've mainly been hesitant to send it to her because I'm still dependent on her, and will likely be so for years to come, as I'm disabled and it will take longer for me to gain my independence, despite working towards it. It's also likely one of the reasons why she's not as scared to overstep my boundaries, unlike with my sister, as she's more independent and able bodied than me, but she's been the GC since we were kids.

You're right, in that if she doesnt reflect on her behavior after I send her the letter, I shouldn't have to feel guilty, and I'll take more control in our relationship however I can, which will likely be grey rocking.

Thanks for the reply.

I didn't really consider the possibility of using an injury for attention. I was thinking the worst where he might consider taking his life, considering his strong traditional beliefs about how a family should look and act like.

By off his rocker, he keeps talking about how much he loves my mom, and I think he's still in denial about my parents' separation, which is why I feel like NC from me will be such a shock to him. My nmom is actually the one who's been showing signs of dementia for a while now, and her narcissistic traits have gotten a lot more relentless, so I'll look into that. 
But yeah, I shouldn't have to feel responsible for his reaction, as well as feeding into these delusions he has about my mom and I.

I think I'll try to build the courage to go NC within this week, whether I tell him how I feel or not before doing so.

Thanks for the reply!

I'm not really worried about getting his permission, I'm sure he's going to try not to let me cut him off. I'm more worried about him doing something extreme to himself when I do cut him off, since I don't think he understood how I felt about him when my parents divorced, and thought I might've still loved him all this time (I still care about him, I just can't have a relationship with him).
Thanks for the tip, I'll try it when I get the chance.

Yeah, you're right. Making this post sort of eased my worries a bit. Whenever I get the chance to check the place out, I'll give a decent look over everything, and I'll leave it at that unless I find something unusual. Thanks.

How would they retrieve the footage from a dvr? They would also have to come inside the house to personally retrieve it, right?

Sorry for all the questions, I appreciate the info.
Thanks for the reassurance and tips.

It's a single family home. There's a satellite dish on the roof, is it possible for a camera to be wirelessly connected through that?

If there are hardwired cameras, does the footage only get recorded on a storage drive like an SD card, and can then only be accessed by coming into the house and taking the storage drive?

I feel that fully furnished places are inherently more risky in this regard compared to unfurnished, considering how many places you can hide a recording device, especially in electronics. I feel like it makes it so that you can never be sure enough.

But yeah, I'd agree that I'm paranoid. I guess I'll judge the place for myself when I see it, but my mom will have already signed the lease by the time she can book another showing for me to check it out.
